excerpt: A Post and Courier analysis of 2011–2015 collision data recorded 629 crashes at the Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 intersection in North Charleston — about one every three days, the most of any intersection in the tri-county area and second in the state. Here's why, and what your rights are if you're injured there.
keyTakeaways: A Post and Courier analysis of 2011–2015 collision data recorded 629 crashes at Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 in North Charleston — about one every three days, more than at any other intersection in the tri-county area and second in the state behind I-20 at US-176 in Columbia. None of those 629 crashes was fatal, though 181 people were injured. High-speed off-ramp traffic, complex left turns, and commercial density are the primary factors. Under S.C. Code § 15-3-530, injured victims have 3 years to file suit. Government entities like SCDOT may share liability for design deficiencies under the South Carolina Tort Claims Act.

faqs.question: How often do crashes occur at Ashley Phosphate & I-26?
faqs.answer: A Post and Courier analysis of 2011–2015 collision data recorded 629 crashes at the Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 intersection — roughly one every three days. That was more than at any other intersection in Berkeley, Charleston or Dorchester counties, and second in the state behind I-20 at US-176 in Columbia. Worth noting alongside the frequency: none of those 629 crashes was fatal, though 181 people were injured.

faqs.question: What makes the Ashley Phosphate/I-26 intersection so dangerous?
faqs.answer: Five primary factors: vehicles exiting I-26 at highway speed encountering a red light within a short distance, complex left-turn movements across multiple lanes, commercial density on all four corners generating constant turning conflicts, long signal cycles that encourage red-light running, and traffic volume that far exceeds the intersection's design capacity.

faqs.question: Who is responsible for crashes caused by dangerous intersection design?
faqs.answer: Under the South Carolina Tort Claims Act, the city of North Charleston and SCDOT may bear liability for intersection design deficiencies they knew or should have known about. Given the well-documented crash data at Ashley Phosphate/I-26, a strong argument exists that the responsible agencies have been on notice of the danger. These claims require strict notice compliance — contact an attorney promptly.

faqs.question: What should I do after an accident at Ashley Phosphate & I-26?
faqs.answer: Call 911 for a police report, seek immediate medical attention at Trident Medical Center, photograph the scene (including signal positions and vehicle locations), get witness contact information, do not give recorded statements to insurance companies, and contact a personal injury attorney who can preserve traffic camera footage and signal timing data before it is overwritten.
